newsitem.title: CHINA: China says holds no political prisoners.
newsitem.headline: China says holds no political prisoners.

text.p: China lauded its human rights record on Tuesday, saying political prisoners did not exist in the authoritarian communist state.
"So-called political prisoners do not exist in China," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told reporters at a regular news briefing.
"Of course, because of violations of certain Chinese laws, there have been those who have been convicted and punished, but this does not mean they are political prisoners," Shen said.

China jailed dozens of political dissidents in 1996 as part of a drive to ensure stability and amid an easing of foreign pressure over its human rights record, diplomats and human rights activists have said.
Beijing has used broad anti-subversion laws to prosecute and imprison those it sees as challenging the Communist Party's grip on power.

China had made great progress in improving its human rights record since the 1949 communist takeover and especially since the launching of market-oriented reforms by current paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, Shen said.
"The Chinese government has made efforts...to promote and protect human rights and basic freedoms," Shen said.
Shen lashed out at U.S. critics of Beijing's human rights record, saying such people were misinformed or ignorant of China's actual situation.
"Some people in the United States are biased against China and don't understand it," he said, adding that U.S. reports on abuses of basic freedoms in China were interference in its internal affairs.
"In the questions of human rights and law, China and the United States should step up communication and dialogue on the basis of mutual respect," he said.
The U.S. State Department releases an annual report on human rights abuses worldwide and has been particularly critical of China for its suppression of political dissent.

Beijing angrily rejects such criticism and points to rapid economic growth and rising standards of living as evidence that it is guarding the basic rights of its 1.2 billion people to food and clothing.
